construct: IgG antibodies against presynaptic P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channels reduce calcium entry and acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction. Repeated activation temporarily increases presynaptic calcium, producing facilitation of strength and reflexes; autonomic dysfunction is common and the syndrome is strongly associated with small-cell lung cancer.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Proximal weakness, autonomic symptoms, depressed reflexes that facilitate after contraction, and a likely small-cell lung cancer identify Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Myasthenia gravis is the strongest neuromuscular-junction alternative, but it is postsynaptic, generally preserves reflexes and autonomic function, and typically worsens rather than facilitates with repeated use.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Autonomic dysfunction plus exercise-induced reflex facilitation and a hilar mass make Lambert-Eaton the unique diagnosis.
